title: sdd audit verifies citations against files the plan's own author wrote, ignored files and the plan itself
desc:
audit._check reads the raw working tree (audit.py _check / _resolve). Reproduced in a temp repo with audit.run():
- a citation to an untracked file created in the same session (src/fake.py) verifies ok -- a model can invent a line, write it to disk, cite it and pass
- a citation to a gitignored file (scratch/n.txt) verifies ok
- a citation to .workflow/<KEY>/sdd.json -- the plan citing itself -- verifies ok
_resolve only refuses paths outside the repo.

ACCEPTANCE:
- the first (strict) audit resolves citations against committed content (HEAD via gitctx.file_at), not the working tree
- a citation into .workflow/** is refused with its own verdict and detail
- a citation into an ignored or untracked path is refused; a file the plan lists as change: add cannot serve as evidence
- re-audits (under_way) keep the current baseline/moved behaviour for committed files
- each case has a regression test that fails before the fix
